post.caption: Gold hid under an uneven floor. In the late 1980s, Iraqi archaeologists led by Muzahim Mahmoud Hussein dug at Nimrud, an Assyrian city. They noticed a part of the palace floor that looked uneven, though Agatha Christie's husband, Max Mallowan, had already dug there. Under it lay four royal tombs of Assyrian queens with hundreds of gold pieces about 2,700 years old. One tomb held 79 gold earrings and 30 finger rings. A queen's crown shows grapes and winged spirits, some bracelets were joined to rings, and a single gold anklet weighs about a kilo.
